newsitem.title: USA: SEC seeks Grigsby campaign gift records in Calif..
newsitem.headline: SEC seeks Grigsby campaign gift records in Calif..

text.p: A Securities and Exchange Commission official in Florida has asked California state campaign contribution regulators for campaign contribution information about the former chairman of investment banking firm Grigsby Brandford & Co Inc.

An official in the SEC Miami office asked the California Fair Political Practices Commission Monday for information about Calvin Grigsby, who resigned as chairman earlier this month, government sources in California said Wednesday.
Charles Senatore, the SEC's regional director in Miami, declined to comment.
An SEC official in California also declined to comment.

The SEC official in Miami asked for a copy of a recent settlement between the California commission and Grigsby. SEC also asked the commission if it had any information about campaign contributions by Grigsby to Florida public officials.
The California commission sent a copy of the settlement to SEC in Miami and told the SEC official that the commission does not have jurisdiction over out-of-state contributions.
The Miami Herald newspaper reported last week that Grigsby resigned after federal prosecutors from Miami interviewed him in California about Dade County, Fla., bond deals.
Grigsby's resignation was announced amid questions over a $183 million Dade County revenue bond refinancing.
His departure also came a week after it was disclosed that Grigsby paid a $5,000 fine for making campaign contributions in California without complete disclosure.

The California Fair Political Practices Commission said Grigsby made campaign contributions totaling $11,500 in the first half of 1993. During the second half of 1993, Fiscal Funding Co Inc and other entities controled by Grigsby made campaign contributions totaling $42,000.

The California commission said Grigsby and Fiscal Funding failed to file timely major donor campaign statements reporting these contributions. Grigsby is a 50 percent owner and controling partner of Fiscal Funding, an equipment leasing company.
The campaign contributions outlined by the California commission took place before Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board's Rule G-37 was enacted in April 1994.
MSRB's Rule G-37 bars municipal dealers that make contributions to issuer clients from doing business for two years with those governments.
SEC, which oversees MSRB activities, brought its first charges against an underwriter March 7 for violations of Rule G-37.
The California Fair Political Practices Commission enforces state rules that deal with political contributions and conflicts of interest.
Grigsby Brandford is one of the largest minority-owned municipal bond underwriters in the U.S. It did not return phone messages Wednesday.
